Notre client est une très grande organisation publique, avec plusieurs milliers de collaborateurs. Ces opportunités long terme (plusieurs années) nécessitent une présence régulière sur Genève (ou dans la région frontalière).




Ces rôles sont pour des consultants (Permanent ou Freelance) intéressés à rejoindre un grand projet dans la région de Genève. Nous nous occupons de toute la partie administrative (payroll, permis, administration et relocation le cas échéant).




LE ROLE


Au sein du service Développement sur-mesure, vous renforcez la capacité de développement des équipes produit en charge d'applications Java utilisées par différents offices. Vous êtes autonome sur l'ensemble du cycle de développement (conception, réalisation, tests, intégration, déploiement) et attaché(e) à la qualité logicielle, à la sécurité applicative et à la confidentialité des données. Deux positions sont à pourvoir. Technologies de la filière: Java, Spring Boot, Hibernate / JPA, API REST, PostgreSQL, GitLab CI, Docker, OpenShift.



  • Concevoir, développer et maintenir des applications et composants Java dans le respect des standards de la filière.

  • Concevoir et réaliser les tests (unitaires, intégration, acceptation) et les automatiser dans la chaîne CI/CD.

  • Pratiquer la revue de code systématique et contribuer à la documentation technique.

  • Analyser et corriger les anomalies lors des phases de tests d'intégration et fonctionnels.

  • Garantir le niveau de qualité et de sécurité du code livré: indicateurs SonarQube, remédiation des vulnérabilités, protection des données.

  • Identifier et communiquer les risques et problèmes, fédérer les personnes concernées pour rechercher des solutions.

  • Participer à l'amélioration continue des pratiques d'ingénierie, des outils et de l'organisation Agile de l'équipe, et partager l'expérience acquise au sein des communautés de pratiques.




Démarrage prévu en février 2027.






Requirements
VOTRE PROFIL



  • Diplôme d'ingénieur ou Master (ou équivalent) en informatique.

  • 6 ans et plus d'expérience.

  • Java: maîtrise du langage (versions LTS récentes) et des principes de conception objet (SOLID, design patterns).

  • Backend: Spring et Spring Boot, Hibernate / JPA, application autonome avec serveur intégré.

  • API: conception et développement d'API REST (JAX-RS, OpenAPI), sécurisation avec OAuth2 / OIDC.

  • Architecture hexagonale, séparation frontend / backend, connaissance des concepts d'architecture logicielle courants.

  • Qualité logicielle: tests unitaires et d'intégration (JUnit), TDD / BDD (Cucumber, Gherkin), revue de code systématique, SonarQube.

  • Sécurité applicative et confidentialité des données: OWASP Top 10, gestion des secrets, protection des données personnelles et sensibles.

  • DevOps: Git et GitFlow, GitLab CI, Maven, Docker, OpenShift. Bases de données relationnelles et SQL (PostgreSQL). Expérience confirmée en Agile / Scrum et JIRA.

  • Important: messagerie asynchrone (AsyncAPI, RabbitMQ), DDD, microservices, frontend (TypeScript, Web Components, SPA), AppSec (SAST / DAST / SCA), modernisation d'applications existantes (Java ancien, EJB / Struts, JBoss / Tomcat, Oracle), Kubernetes.

  • Un plus: publication de code en open source, outils d'IA d'assistance au développement, Vue.js ou React, Nginx, Express, Dynatrace, Splunk, expérience confirmée dans une administration publique.

  • Qualités: autonomie, responsabilité, adaptabilité, esprit d'équipe, partage des connaissances, rigueur et discrétion, capacité à travailler sous pression.






Benefits
C'est une excellente opportunité de rejoindre une large entité genevoise sur le long terme et de participer à un grand projet de transformation.

Hey there!
We’re Fever, the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.

Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.

Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.

Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?

To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!

Ready to be part of the experience?

Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.

We are looking for a Senior Product Engineer to join our Data Team. This is a role for an engineer who cares deeply about product impact, user experience, and how systems connect to real business outcomes. You will work across the full stack, from the interfaces users interact with to the services and data layers that power them, and bridge the gap between our AI and data capabilities and the products people actually use. You won't just take tickets and ship code. You'll own features end-to-end: shaping the problem with Product and Design, building it, defining success metrics, and iterating based on real data. If you thrive in ambiguous, high-leverage environments, love shipping with judgment, and want your engineering work to be visibly tied to outcomes that matter, you'll fit right in.

Tech environment

This role is intentionally not defined by one framework or specialty. That said, you will likely operate across the full stack: a modern TypeScript web platform where several frontends and frameworks coexist, and where moving between them matters more than allegiance to one, that also ships inside our native apps through webviews and a native/web bridge; Python-based services and APIs; relational, NoSQL, and search datastores, data warehouses, and SQL; event-driven and distributed systems; cloud infrastructure, containers, and CI/CD pipelines; and observability tooling. Depending on the project, you may also work with LLM APIs and agent-based workflows, retrieval patterns, data orchestration, and product analytics and A/B experimentation.

Nice to have

  • Strong TypeScript and depth in at least one modern web framework. Our web platform is a large monorepo combining several frontends, where Angular and Astro/Svelte coexist. Comfort moving across frameworks matters more than allegiance to one.
  • Strong componentization skills: designing reusable components and shared modules whose logic lives in framework-agnostic packages, including web features that ship inside our native apps through webviews and JavaScript/native bridges. Our apps are Kotlin/Jetpack Compose and Swift/SwiftUI; you won't own them, but you'll integrate deeply with them.
  • Sound judgment on when to render server-side vs client-side (or hybrid), driven by functional and non-functional requirements such as SEO, performance, personalization, and caching, rather than framework defaults.
  • Experience working on internal platforms, operational tools, or product-heavy backend systems.
  • Experience with Python frameworks such as Django or FastAPI.
  • Experience with PostgreSQL, Snowflake, DynamoDB, Redis, OpenSearch, and SQL-heavy applications.
  • Familiarity with event-driven architectures or messaging systems such as Kafka or RabbitMQ.
  • Experience with AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, or similar infrastructure patterns.
  • Familiarity with observability and monitoring tooling (Datadog or similar).
  • Exposure to AI-enabled product development: LLM integrations, agent frameworks (LangGraph/LangChain), LLM observability (Langfuse), RAG patterns, or workflow automation.
  • Familiarity with Google Analytics 4 and Google Tag Manager. Product tracking at Fever runs through Dataverse, our in-house unified behavioural event layer built on server-side GTM, so knowing how GA and GTM work is enough to find your way around. We also use Mixpanel.
  • Familiarity with product experimentation: A/B testing, feature flags, and edge-side experimentation. We bucket anonymous users and run rollouts at the CDN edge (CloudFront Functions), with Statsig and Optimizely as the experimentation platforms.
  • Experience working on 0 to 1 initiatives or undefined problem spaces.
  • Demonstrated leadership through ownership of difficult projects with broad impact.

What success looks like

  • You turn ambiguous opportunities into working systems or products that create clear value.
  • You help teams make better trade-offs and avoid overengineering, fragmentation, and local optimization.
  • You improve not only what gets built, but also how decisions are made.
  • You become a trusted technical leader for important cross-functional initiatives.
  • You increase the leverage of other engineers and teams through your judgment, technical direction, and execution support.
  • You help connect engineering work to real operational and business outcomes.

Who will thrive in this role

You will likely thrive here if:

  • You are energized by ambitious, messy, high-leverage problems.
  • You like operating where priorities evolve and the path is not fully defined.
  • You care more about impact than about staying inside a narrowly defined engineering lane.
  • You enjoy combining engineering depth, product thinking, and business context.
  • You naturally look for the highest-leverage way to move a system, a team, or a product forward.
  • You want to play a meaningful role in shaping how the company builds and scales.

Why join Fever

  • You will work on some of the company's most strategic problems.
  • You will have real ownership and visible impact.
  • You will help shape products, systems, and capabilities that matter across the business.
  • You will work in an environment that values ambition, adaptability, pragmatism, and execution.
  • You will be surrounded by smart, driven people who care about building things that matter.

Benefits & Perks

  • Flexible schedule
  • Bonus
  • Stock options
  • 40% discount on all Fever events and experiences
  • Health insurance from Day 1
  • English or Spanish Lessons
  • Wellhub Membership
  • Cobee (tax free allowance on restaurants and transport)
  • Possibility to receive in advance part of your salary by Payflow

Thank you for considering joining Fever. We cannot wait to learn more about you!

If you want to learn more about us: Fever's Blog | Tech.Eu |TechCrunch

Fever is committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workspace where everyone's background and ideas count. Our main goal is to find the best possible talent regardless of place of birth, racial or ethnic origin, gender, gender identity, religion, opinion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, marital status, age or caring responsibilities. We encourage everyone to apply!

If you require any kind of accommodation during the selection process please contact our Talent team so we can help you by providing a welcoming and seamless journey.

Doctolib is becoming an AI-native company. We are redesigning the way we work, workflow by workflow, and are looking for people who will not only support this transformation, but actively build it. As a Senior AI Specialist, you will be the technical builder and AI Ops Owner behind AI-powered productivity for our Operations and Customer Success teams.

 

You will work in founder and product mode: you will own a workflow end to end, from context and agent design to evaluation, and continuously take it to a higher level of automation. Our ambition is to move away from manual case-by-case work towards workflows that run largely autonomously while maintaining a high quality bar. In this way, you will contribute directly to our mission of improving healthcare for everyone.

Your Responsibilities

  • Redesign workflows rather than simply automating them: You analyze the most critical Operations and Customer Success workflows, break down time-consuming processes that require limited judgment, and transform them through the use of AI agents. You set clear objectives for autonomy and quality, and continuously develop them further.

  • Build and operate AI agents as products: You develop and manage agents on platforms such as Dust or Claude. Each agent is deployed to production with a defined baseline and relevant metrics such as benefit, usage, and scalability.

  • Knowledge and context management: You deliberately curate the context agents need, from templates to core data. The guiding principle is quality over quantity. You ensure that knowledge sources in Confluence, Drive, or Salesforce are always up to date and well structured.

  • Evaluation and quality assurance: You define quality standards and establish evaluation routines to identify and address weaknesses such as hallucinations or prompt drift at an early stage. You continuously optimize prompts through systematic user feedback and A/B testing.

  • CRM and data integration: You own the interfaces between CRM systems such as Salesforce and our AI platforms. You automate data flows and work closely with IT to unlock new, valuable data sources for our agents.

  • Central interface and enablement: You translate business requirements into technical solutions and bring together stakeholders from Leadership, IT, and Product. You strengthen the team’s AI fluency in the areas of context, agent management, and evaluation.

  • Impact and measurement: Rather than inventing new KPIs, you make the success of AI measurable using existing metrics such as time, quality, and cost, and use these insights to guide the next steps in scaling.

Your Profile

Since production-ready AI workflows and agent technologies are still relatively new, years of market experience are rare. We therefore deliberately prioritize potential over years of experience alone. What matters to us is your ability to learn quickly, your strong product mindset, and your judgment.   • Technical and data understanding: You can read and adapt scripts, understand APIs, webhooks, and automation tools such as Make, n8n, and Zapier, and know how CRM data, ideally Salesforce data, flows into AI systems.

  • Strong communication skills: You have a confident command of English and can operate at the highest level in our international environment. German at B1 level is sufficient.

  • Expertise with agent platforms: You have practical experience with systems such as Dust, Claude, or LangChain. Since tools evolve quickly, we primarily rely on your process understanding and evaluation skills as a sustainable foundation.

About Kestra

Kestra is the universal orchestration platform: open source, declarative, and designed to orchestrate data pipelines, IT automation, business workflows, and AI/agentic systems.

Trusted by over 10,000 organizations worldwide, including JPMorgan Chase, Bloomberg, FILA, and Crédit Agricole, Kestra orchestrates mission-critical workloads at scale. The open-source project has close to 30,000 GitHub stars, hundreds of contributors, and a fast-growing global community.

About the role

Kestra runs arbitrary, user-defined code at scale. Our users write workflows that execute scripts, containers, and queries against their own production systems, through hundreds of community-built plugins, on a platform whose entire source code is public. That is an unusually rich attack surface, and securing it is a genuinely hard engineering problem rather than a checklist exercise.
You would be our first dedicated security hire. We're looking for a Senior Security Engineer to own and elevate the end-to-end security posture of our platform, infrastructure, and open-source ecosystem.
This is a unique, hybrid role for someone who excels at both sides of security: actively breaking systems to find vulnerabilities (hands-on penetration testing) and actively fixing them (opening PRs, patching infrastructure, and managing supply chain risks). If you want to build a world-class security foundation for a fast-growing open-source and SaaS platform, this role is for you.
This is a hands-on engineering role, not a GRC or compliance one.

What you would do

Your first six months would focus on the first three points below. The rest is where the role grows.

  • Conduct hands-on penetration testing and threat modeling across our web application, APIs, control plane, and cloud environments.

  • Manage end-to-end vulnerability tracking across our codebases, software dependencies (SCA), container images, and cloud infrastructure.

  • Proactively fix security flaws by writing patches, submitting Pull Requests (PRs), or collaborating directly with product teams to guide remediation.

  • Audit and harden our cloud infrastructure (GCP, Kubernetes clusters, and networking configurations) against external and internal threats.

  • Automate security tooling into our CI/CD pipelines (SAST, DAST, dependency scanners) to catch CVEs before code reaches production.

  • Perform security code reviews and evaluate third-party dependencies, open-source integrations, and supply-chain risks.

  • Lead incident response efforts and establish continuous monitoring, detection, and mitigation strategies.

  • Own our public security posture as an open-source project: vulnerability disclosure process, CVE handling, security advisories, and the trust model of our plugin ecosystem.

Our Tech Stack

  • Security & Vulnerability Tools: Trivy, GitHub Security / Dependabot, Elastic Security

  • Infrastructure: Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform

  • Cloud: GCP

  • Programming language: Java, Typescript, Javascript

  • Datastore: PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch

  • Queuing: Redis, Kafka, AMQP

  • Monitoring & Logs: ELK, Prometheus, Grafana

  • Deployment & Repository: GitHub Actions, ArgoCD

What we are looking for

  • 5+ years of experience in Security Engineering, Product Security, DevSecOps, or a combined Offensive/Defensive role.

  • Strong hands-on penetration testing background, with proven ability to discover application, API, and network-level vulnerabilities.

  • A builder/fixer mindset: You don't just export scanner PDFs; you can read code, understand exploits, write fixes, or provide clear remediation steps to engineers.

  • Deep familiarity with cloud security (AWS or GCP) and containerized environments (Kubernetes, Docker).

  • Experience with dependency and supply-chain security (CVE management, open-source licensing, SCA tools).

  • Fluent in English and comfortable working autonomously in a fully remote environment.

  • Adaptability to a fast-paced open-source startup environment where pragmatism and execution speed matter.

Perks & Benefits

  • Work from anywhere: We’re a remote-first company, so you can work from wherever feels like home. Plus, you’ll have access to coworking spaces worldwide if you ever need a change of scenery.

  • Health coverage: From medical support, dental, and vision, we've got you covered.

  • Home office setup on us: We’ll provide all the equipment you need to work comfortably.

     

Our Hiring Process

We aim to move quickly (2-3 weeks), but we can adjust the timeline if needed.

  • Intro call with the hiring manager (30 min)

  • Technical scenario / Practical assessment (2 hours, asynchronous homework focusing on threat assessment and remediation)

  • Team chat with one of your future colleagues (30 min)

  • Final discussion with one of our co-founders (30 min)

Chez Stoïk, la tech construit l'ensemble des produits qui font tourner notre modèle : de la distribution de nos contrats d'assurance et de nos outils cyber jusqu'aux applications utilisées par nos assurés au quotidien.

L'équipe Est Organisée En Squads Autonomes, Chacune Composée D'un PM, D'un Designer Et De Développeurs TypeScript, Regroupées En Deux Tribes

Distribution

: la squad Insurance Distribution développe la plateforme de distribution assurance utilisée par nos courtiers (quote, questionnaire de risque, contrats, polices), la squad Cyber Distribution gère la distribution de nos solutions cyber via nos partenaires MSP, et la squad Platform, transverse aux deux, prend en charge la facturation, les reportings et les outils internes.

Security

: la tribe développe Stoïk Protect, la plateforme de cybersécurité utilisée au quotidien par nos clients et assurés pour évaluer et réduire leur exposition aux risques cyber (scans de vulnérabilités, simulations de phishing, sensibilisation des collaborateurs), avec un fort enjeu produit et UX pour rendre la cybersécurité accessible à des entreprises sans expertise technique.

Notre enjeu commun : rendre des domaines intrinsèquement complexes (assurance, cybersécurité, réglementation européenne) les plus simples et les plus scalables possible, pour vendre toujours plus de produits, sur toujours plus de marchés, sans jamais complexifier le produit.

Ton impact au quotidien

Au sein de ta squad, tu interviens sur l'ensemble du cycle de vie du produit :

Architecture & Build

: Concevoir et implémenter des fonctionnalités robustes dans notre monorepo, structuré selon les principes de la Clean Architecture.

Simplicité & scalabilité

: Transformer une logique métier complexe en parcours simples et en briques réutilisables, pensées pour de nouveaux produits et de nouveaux marchés.

Product mindset

: Porter tes features de bout en bout, en travaillant main dans la main avec les PMs et Designers : challenger les specs et les designs, développer en fullstack, tester, échanger avec les stakeholders, itérer après la mise en prod.

Internationalisation

: Concevoir des produits capables d'absorber les spécificités des différents marchés européens sur lesquels nous opérons.

L’IA au cœur de notre façon de travailler

L’IA Fait Partie Intégrante De Notre Façon De Construire Le Produit, Et C’est Un Vrai Levier Pour Toute L’équipe

Pour développer

: agents de code, challenge des specs, revue de code assistée. On cherche en permanence à aller plus vite sans baisser le niveau d’exigence.

Over Nedlin

Nedlin is een industriële textielverzorger voor Healthcare, Hospitality en Industry, waar veiligheid, kwaliteit, continu verbeteren en verantwoord ondernemen centraal staan. Als groeiend B-Corp familiebedrijf investeren we graag in jong talent en versterken we de verbinding tussen onderwijs en arbeidsmarkt. Daarom bieden we studenten de kans om praktijkervaring op te doen, zich te ontwikkelen en Nedlin te leren kennen, met waar mogelijk mooie doorgroeikansen na het afstuderen.

De stageopdracht

Tijdens deze hbo-stage ga je aan de slag met Lock Out Tag Out (LOTO). LOTO is een veiligheidsmethode waarbij machines en energiebronnen tijdens onderhoud of werkzaamheden veilig worden uitgeschakeld en vergrendeld. Zo wordt voorkomen dat een machine onverwacht wordt ingeschakeld terwijl eraan wordt gewerkt. Jij helpt Nedlin om deze werkwijze verder te ontwikkelen, te standaardiseren en praktisch toepasbaar te maken.

  • Je onderzoekt de huidige LOTO-werkwijze en brengt risico’s, energiebronnen en isolatiepunten in kaart.

  • Je ontwikkelt een uniforme LOTO-procedure en machine-specifieke LOTO-kaarten.

  • Je brengt de benodigde materialen en hulpmiddelen in kaart.

  • Je ontwikkelt instructie- en toolboxmateriaal voor medewerkers.

  • Je stelt een praktisch implementatieadvies op om LOTO binnen Nedlin verder te borgen.

Wat bieden wij?

  • Stagevergoeding:

    • € 300,- bruto per maand voor mbo-studenten (op basis van 40 uur per week);

    • € 400,- bruto per maand voor hbo-studenten (op basis van 40 uur per week);

  • Een leerzame stage binnen één van de modernste en duurzaamste wasserijen van Europa;

  • Ruimte en begeleiding om te werken aan jouw (afstudeer)opdracht;

  • Persoonlijke begeleiding en korte lijnen;

  • Een familiaire en positieve sfeer: samen feestdagen vieren, een jaarlijkse familiedag en leuke uitjes;

  • Kans op een (bij)baan bij Nedlin na afronding van je stage, bij wederzijdse match.

Veiligheid tijdens je stage

Veiligheid staat ook tijdens de uitvoering van de stageopdracht voorop. Je voert daarom geen risicovolle onderhoudswerkzaamheden zelfstandig uit. Eventuele technische aanpassingen worden uitsluitend uitgevoerd door bevoegde medewerkers of externe partijen. Machinekaarten worden vóór ingebruikname gevalideerd door de Technische Dienst.


Wie ben jij?

  • Je volgt een hbo-opleiding, bijvoorbeeld Integrale Veiligheidskunde, Technische Bedrijfskunde, Werktuigbouwkunde, Elektrotechniek, Engineering of Facility Management.

  • Je hebt interesse in techniek en veiligheid en combineert graag theorie met praktijk.

  • Je werkt zelfstandig, nauwkeurig en proactief en communiceert gemakkelijk met collega’s.

  • Je bent 32 tot 40 uur per week beschikbaar voor een meewerk- en/of afstudeerstage.

  • Je kunt zelfstandig naar onze locatie in Elsloo of Hoensbroek reizen.

Mission

  • Nice, minimal layout.

Roles & rules

  • Have two roles:

  • admin:

    • Can remove any listing, view all loans, and mark a lender as “Trusted Lender”.

  • user:

    • Can create, edit, and delete only their own listings, and act only on requests involving their own tools or their own borrowing.

  • Implement the above role-based access control with best practices, enforced in Convex functions, not only in the UI.

Automation with n8n

  • Build at least two n8n workflows:

  • Request notification: when a borrow request is created or changes status, Convex calls an n8n Webhook. The workflow notifies the relevant user (email, Slack, Discord, or a logged mock notification is fine) using only the fields it needs.

  • Overdue reminders: a scheduled workflow runs daily, fetches overdue loans from a Convex HTTP endpoint, sends a reminder to each borrower, and writes the reminder status back to Convex.

  • Secure the integration in both directions:

  • Sign webhook payloads (e.g. HMAC with a shared secret) and verify signatures on the receiving side.

  • Keep secrets in environment variables and n8n credentials, never in code or exported workflow JSON.

  • Make write-backs idempotent so retries do not create duplicate records or reminders.

  • Handle failures with retries and an error workflow (or equivalent) so failed runs are visible and never fail silently.

  • (Bonus) Show recent automation activity on each loan in the app, e.g. “Reminder sent 2 days ago”.

Deliverables

  • Exported n8n workflow JSON files in the repository.

  • A README covering local setup (including n8n, e.g. a docker-compose file), environment variables, architecture, and your security and data-minimization decisions.

  • A short note on what you would change to run this in production.

About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer on the Applied AI team at Nebius Token Factory, you will own model and endpoint optimization from model artifacts through production deployment. Your work will span model internals, quantization and model compression, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, inference engines, serving architecture, and benchmarking to improve latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, and cost per token while preserving quality and reliability.

You will work with kernel and platform engineers to investigate serving problems, compare configurations, and resolve performance and quality regressions. You will evaluate model- and engine-level optimizations together with distributed inference designs, including request routing, scheduling, prefill/decode coordination, and multi-node GPU execution. Your improvements will be validated through reproducible benchmarks and safe production rollouts under real-world workloads.

Your responsibilities

  • Own optimization projects for specific model families, customer endpoints, or serving backends.
  • Compare inference engines and recommend serving configurations suited to individual workloads.
  • Diagnose model-quality and performance regressions during production rollouts.
  • Improve LLM and VLM endpoint latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, quality, and cost per token.
  • Deploy, configure, benchmark, and extend engines such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, and NVIDIA Dynamo.
  • Develop production model-compression workflows covering quantization, quantization-aware training, distillation, low-bit serving, and accuracy recovery.
  • Implement or integrate speculative decoding, draft-model approaches, KV-cache optimization, prefix caching, chunked prefill, continuous batching, and disaggregated prefill/decode serving. For prefill–decode disaggregation (PDD), evaluate KV-cache transfer, worker placement, and capacity balancing to determine which workloads benefit from the architecture.
  • Design and improve LLM request routers and scheduling policies that balance worker utilization, queueing, request characteristics, and KV-cache locality while meeting latency and reliability targets.
  • Scale dense and mixture-of-experts inference across multiple GPU nodes. Select and tune tensor, pipeline, data, and expert parallelism—including wide expert parallelism (WideEP)—with attention to hardware topology, expert load balance, and communication overhead.
  • Build reproducible benchmark harnesses measuring TTFT, TPOT, tokens per second per GPU, p95/p99 latency, GPU memory, reliability, and cost per token. Validate architecture choices under representative traffic and consistent GPU budgets.
  • Collaborate with GPU kernel and platform engineers to trace bottlenecks across model code, kernels, runtime, scheduler, gateway, and cluster layers.
  • Produce design documents, performance reports, rollout plans, and customer-facing technical explanations.

Must-haves

  • Strong engineering skills in Python and PyTorch.
  • Hands-on experience deploying or optimizing LLM, VLM, or high-throughput transformer inference.
  • Practical knowledge of at least one modern inference stack, such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, NVIDIA Dynamo, Ray Serve, KServe, or an equivalent internal system.
  • A strong understanding of transformer inference bottlenecks involving KV cache, attention, memory bandwidth, batching, parallelism, and long-context serving.
  • Ability to quantify trade-offs among latency, throughput, quality, utilization, and cost.
  • Experience designing or optimizing distributed inference system architecture, with hands-on work in one or more areas such as request routing, distributed scheduling, PDD, multi-node inference, or expert parallelism.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills across research, kernel, infrastructure, product, and customer teams.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience with quantization-aware training, post-training quantization, FP8, INT8, INT4, NVFP4, MXFP4, AWQ, GPTQ, or SmoothQuant.
  • Experience with distillation, speculative decoding, EAGLE, Medusa, multi-token prediction, or related inference acceleration methods.
  • Experience supporting agentic workloads involving tool calling, structured outputs, streaming APIs, high concurrency, and multi-step orchestration.
  • Familiarity with CUDA or Triton; the role does not require kernel engineering to be the candidate’s primary specialization.
  • Contributions to open-source projects such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, FlashInfer, LMCache, PyTorch, Triton, Ray, or KServe.
  • Implementation experience with cache-aware request routing, PDD, or WideEP, including diagnosing communication bottlenecks and load imbalance.
  • Familiarity with GPU communication libraries and interconnects, such as NCCL, NVLink, InfiniBand, or RoCE.

You might know us as ZnanyLekarz in Poland or Doctoralia in Spain. Globally, we are Docplanner.

We build technology that helps people live longer, healthier lives. Our products connect patients with doctors, power clinical workflows, and support healthcare systems used by millions of people every month.

Engineering at Docplanner is about building reliable, scalable systems with real human impact. What we ship affects patients, doctors, and clinics in everyday, high-stakes situations - which means quality, judgment, and long-term thinking matter.

In 2026, we are accelerating delivery across multiple product areas by changing how we build - leveraging AI-assisted development to increase engineering effectiveness and raise the bar on how we design, ship, and evolve systems.

And why should you join us?

Because it feels good to tell your family and your friends how you made the world a little bit better. You go to bed knowing that what you do matters, and that your talents align with your beliefs.

We want to help people live longer, healthier lives, and that starts with you being you. We believe that taking the diversity of human experience into account makes a better healthcare experience for all . We’re not just different: we embrace diversity. We will encourage you to come to work your whole self. You can decide to work fully remote, or work hybrid with our offices located in Barcelona or Warsaw. This will be dependent on the final team allocation.

Marketplace & Search

Build the next-generation marketplace system by owning the end-to-end journey from agentic discovery to rebooking. You’ll leverage AI search and AI onboarding funnels to unlock new demand and transform one-off bookings into continuous care loops.

Practice Management Systems (PMS)

Build the next generation of software to help doctors globally. Unify the current fragmented reality and leverage AI to reinvent the way to help doctors focus on what matters most: treating the patient.

AI-powered Clinical Tools (Noa Medic)

Design AI-native clinical workflows that move beyond simple scribing to replace end-to-end administrative tasks. You'll build deep PMS/EHR embeddings that become an indispensable daily habit for medical professionals.

Patient & Data Integrations (Noa Patient)

Move beyond the booking button to build a proactive healthcare partner. You'll create the smart connections that blend someone's medical past with their live health data, crafting an AI experience that actually keeps patients coming back. Turn raw data into advice people can use, making Docplanner the one health app they can't live without.

Internally, these challenges map to some of our most ambitious and high-impact initiatives.

  • We build systems that matter and we optimize for clarity, speed, and long-term maintainability.

  • Small autonomous teams that own real product surfaces end-to-end

  • High trust and high ownership from day one

  • Production impact early - even as a junior engineer

  • AI-assisted development as a default workflow

  • We prefer solving problems well over adding unnecessary complexity.

  • Good ideas win regardless of tenure or hierarchy.

Strong problem solving ability. The ability to break down complex systems and find elegant solutions.

Builder mindset. You like creating things that people use.

Intellectual curiosity. You enjoy understanding how systems really work.

Ownership. You treat problems as yours until they are solved.

Pragmatism. You know when to optimize and when to ship.

We value signals over credentials.

Competition programming, open-source work, research, side projects or anything else that shows how you think.

  • Our stack evolves continuously, but currently includes technologies such as:

  • Backend: Node.js, TypeScript

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript

  • Mobile: React Native

  • Infrastructure: AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform

  • Developer tooling: modern CI/CD, observability

  • AI-assisted coding environments built to scale (guardrails, rules, skills, subagents, spec-driven development)

We invest heavily in developer productivity and continuously improve how we design and ship systems.

Collaboration Model

• Open source internal culture - contribute across different services and teams

• Maintainer guidance rather than gatekeeping from senior developers

• Cross-functional ownership of features from conception to deployment

• Living documentation shared across all team members

  • Some reasons engineers choose to stay at Docplanner:

  • Real scale. Millions of users and thousands of healthcare providers across multiple countries.

  • Interesting problems. Distributed systems, search relevance, AI-assisted workflows, complex integrations.

  • Exceptional teammates. Work with talented people across disciplines who raise the bar for everyone.

  • Meaningful mission. Helping people live longer, healthier lives.

  • Solid understanding of data structures, algorithms, complexity, and core software engineering principles.

TL;DR:
We’re looking for a full-stack engineer obsessed with Lovable’s growth engine - turning first touches into daily habits, and daily habits into a thriving ecosystem and real revenue. One sprint you’re shipping onboarding and activation flows; the next you’re crafting distribution rails and monetization features that help builders reach more users and keep them around. You think in React and APIs, but your first instinct is always: does this make users more successful, more often?

Coding skills + excellent taste + growth instincts + product obsession = you.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What we’re looking for

  • 5+ years of experience building and growing user-facing products in high-performing teams, ideally including growth work, marketplaces/platforms, or communities.

  • Strong product sense and UX taste for multi-sided systems with creators, learners, and customers - you can see problems from multiple sides and design for all of them.

  • Comfortable using data, funnels, analytics, attribution, and A/B testing to shape what you build and how you iterate.

  • Skilled at designing, measuring, and iterating experiments, and thorough in setting up growth systems “right” from the start.

  • Experience collaborating across functions (design, marketing, partnerships, support, data) to launch and grow new product surfaces and ecosystems.

  • Enjoys designing reusable growth, ecosystem, and monetization tools that other builders can plug into, with a pragmatic and detail-oriented mindset.

  • Motivated by helping others succeed and by seeing impact through engagement, measurable results, and revenue - you care about the scoreboard as much as the code.

What you’ll do

In one sentence: You will build the growth, ecosystem, and monetization systems that make Lovable - and the apps built on it - sticky, discoverable, and revenue-generating.

  • Ship and iterate activation, monetization and retention experiences that create fast, repeatable value and turn first-time users into long-term fans.

  • Build distribution rails for user apps: SEO and performance, shareable moments, social previews, email and lifecycle journeys, and other growth hooks.

  • Ship marketplace and ecosystem features for publishing, discovering, and reusing apps, templates, components, and services - plus profiles, reviews, and matching between builders and customers.

  • Design and implement monetization and pricing flows: payments, subscriptions, access control, plans, paywalls, billing integration, and revenue-share models that work for creators, customers, and Lovable.

  • Build the analytics and experimentation foundations - events, funnels, attribution, and A/B tests - so the team can understand what works and double down on it.

  • Collaborate closely with design, marketing, partnerships, and support to launch and grow new surfaces across the product and ecosystem.

  • Keep the experience relentlessly Lovable while making growth the engine, not the afterthought.

Our tech stack

We're building with tools that both humans and AI love:

  • Frontend: React

  • Backend: Golang and Rust

  • Cloud: Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, Many LLM providers

  • DevOps & Tooling: Github Actions, Grafana, OTEL, infra-as-code (Terraform)

About your application

Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.

We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

The Role

Motion’s products increasingly rely on data-intensive APIs. Beyond our reporting platform, MCP server, and public endpoints, these APIs now power per-customer environments where AI systems can execute tasks, access customer-specific state, and proactively run analysis. Today, that means Azure VMs running Dockerized workloads and a growing layer of application code which needs to cover everything from functionality to routine updates.

We’re looking for a senior software engineer who loves working at the boundary between product code and infrastructure. This is not a traditional DevOps or SRE role. You’ll spend most of your time writing application code that controls infrastructure primitives: messaging queue abstractions, VM management, data lifecycle, container updates, no-downtime migrations, bootstrapping, permissions, observability, and security.

The right person is comfortable going deep into Linux, containers, networking, and all that jazz, but thinks like a product engineer: shipping reliable systems, choosing pragmatic abstractions, and making complicated runtime behavior feel routine to our customers.

| Our tech stack: Node.js, TypeScript, React, MongoDB, ElasticSearch, Azure, and Pulumi.

  • 🔗 Explore our Engineering at Motion page to learn more about our team, our work, and how we build together.

  • Build and evolve the systems that provision, update, secure, and observe Motion’s agent environments.

  • Evolve our infrastructure-as-code footprint in Pulumi — defining patterns other engineers can build on.
  • Work with Linux systems, mounted persistent storage, OS disks, container boundaries, permissions, logs, and runtime debugging.
  • Participate in a small, high-ownership, cross-functional team with weekly cycles.

  • A pragmatic mindset. You can ship the simple thing when speed matters, while flagging that which needs to evolve later.

  • Award-winning team: We're a low-ego, high-performing team that was just ranked #19 on G2's list of Best Canadian Software Companies for 2026.
  • Team connection:
    • Virtual: Day-to-day, we use Roam, an AI-powered virtual office platform that fosters spontaneous collaboration, drop into meetings or quick chats, and interact with colleagues for a simulated, "live" digital headquarters.

In 2026, with fresh funding ($65M+ total capital raised), we’re building forward from that foundation, taking what we learned to market in a deeply AI-native way.

About Dotfile

Dotfile is building the AI-native Compliance Operating System for financial institutions. Our mission is to make compliance simple, safe and smart, helping financial institutions onboard customers, manage risk and operate globally.

Compliance remains one of the most manual functions in financial services. While most institutions still rely on fragmented tools and human-driven workflows, we believe AI is enabling a fundamental shift toward autonomous compliance. Our ambition is to build Level 5 Compliance: software that can gather evidence, investigate complex situations, assess risk and execute defensible decisions under defined policies.

Dotfile has grown into one of Europe’s fastest-growing compliance technology companies. Today, 100+ financial institutions across 15 countries rely on Dotfile for critical compliance operations, with a rapidly growing presence in the US.

We recently raised our Series A from leading US and European investors and software operators. We’re now entering our next chapter: investing heavily in product and AI, expanding internationally, and building the team that can make Dotfile the global standard for compliance infrastructure.

About The Role

You’ll join an AI-native engineering team where AI is central to how we design, build and ship software. We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer who understands software deeply, uses AI to build better software faster, and wants to help improve how the whole team works.

You will own projects from understanding the customer problem to shipping a solution and improving it in production. Working closely with engineering and product, you will help decide what we build, how we build it, and where to invest as the platform grows.

This is a hands-on role with broad ownership. Your focus will reflect your strengths and the team’s priorities, whether that means building product experiences, developing backend services, or solving challenges across the platform. We value engineers who bring depth in their area and curiosity beyond it.

What You’ll Do

  • Own projects from discovery and technical design through implementation, testing, deployment and follow-up.
  • Work closely with product and other engineers to understand customer needs, challenge assumptions and turn complex requirements into clear, usable software.
  • Build and improve the interfaces, APIs and services that financial institutions rely on for their compliance operations.
  • Make pragmatic technical decisions, balancing delivery speed with reliability, security and maintainability.
  • Investigate production issues and improve performance, observability and resilience as the platform grows.
  • Raise the engineering bar through knowledge sharing and improvements to how we develop and ship software.
  • Contribute to the evolution of our platform as we build more AI-powered compliance capabilities.

About You

  • You have 5+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of delivering and maintaining software in production.
  • You understand software in depth. You bring strong fundamentals and depth in backend or full-stack development. You can reason about data, concurrency, performance and failure modes, and investigate unfamiliar systems beyond the surface.
  • AI coding agents are central to how you work. You use tools such as Codex or Claude Code extensively to explore, build, test and review software. You keep experimenting with ways to make yourself more effective.
  • You bring the judgment that makes AI-assisted development work. You frame problems clearly, provide useful context, challenge assumptions and verify the resulting behavior. You can explain why a solution works and take responsibility for what you ship.
  • You take ownership. You can turn an ambiguous problem into a practical plan, follow through on delivery and improve the result in production. You are comfortable learning new technologies and working beyond your usual area when a problem calls for it.
  • You care about the product as much as the implementation. You want to understand who you are building for, challenge requirements when needed and assess whether your work solves the original problem.
  • You value simple, well-designed solutions. You know when to move quickly and when reliability, security or long-term maintenance require more care.
  • You communicate clearly in English and enjoy collaborating. You explain your technical choices, welcome constructive disagreement and share what you learn with your teammates.
  • You want to help shape an AI-native engineering team. You enjoy improving how software gets built, from reusable agent workflows to better testing and feedback loops, and turning your own discoveries into practices that make the whole team more effective.

Experience in B2B SaaS, fintech or compliance is a plus.

Our technology

Our Main Language Is TypeScript. Our Stack Includes

  • Frontend: React, Apollo GraphQL and Storybook.
  • Backend: Node.js, NestJS, GraphQL and PostgreSQL.
  • Infrastructure: AWS and Kubernetes.
  • Development and testing: Nx, GitLab CI, Playwright.

You do not need experience with every part of our stack. We care about your engineering judgment, your ability to learn and the quality of the software you build.

Why join us

  • Join a company with traction and room to shape its future. With 100+ financial institutions using Dotfile and a recent Series A, you’ll help define the next stage of the product and engineering team.
  • Help shape how an AI-native team works. Experiment with new approaches, improve your own workflow and turn what you learn into practices that make the whole team more effective.
  • Put your engineering depth to work. Solve demanding problems in automation, AI, data and reliability, building software that financial institutions depend on every day.
  • Have a direct say in what you build. Influence technical decisions, own projects through to production, and see how your work changes the customer experience.

Our hiring process

  • CTO conversation — 30-60 minutes : Discuss your background, explore the role and how our engineering team works, and answer technical questions to assess your engineering knowledge and problem-solving approach.
  • Case study — 60 minutes : Design the architecture of a project we provide, or present the architecture of a past project you led. Walk us through your reasoning, technical decisions and trade-offs.
  • Raise the bar — 30 minutes: Meet someone from Product or Solutions Consulting to discuss how you collaborate across teams, understand customer needs and approach problems together.
  • Founder discussion — 15-30 minutes: Meet our CEO to discuss Dotfile’s ambition, what motivates you and the contribution you could make.

Objectif :

Il s'agit de renforcer la gestion des vulnérabilités sur le périmètre Business Applications, d'industrialiser les pratiques DevSecOps et d'assurer une traçabilité complète, dans un environnement international et réglementé. Le poste implique de travailler avec les équipes Dev, Infra, Sécurité, Architecture et Claranet.

Remédiation des vulnérabilités middleware (~80 %)

· Tenir l'inventaire des composants middleware et de leurs versions : runtimes Java et .NET, serveurs web, images de base de conteneurs, Node.js, Amazon Corretto…

· Traiter les résultats des scanners Qualys et MDASH : dédoublonnage, qualification, analyse de l'exploitabilité réelle, puis priorisation selon le CVSS, l'EPSS, le catalogue KEV et l'exposition de l'actif.

· Corriger : montées de version, correctifs de configuration, durcissement, reconstruction et rebasage des images de conteneurs.

· Superviser les tests des correctifs hors production avec les PO et les BRM (Business Relationship Managers), définir les plans de retour arrière et coordonner les mises en production via le Change Management.

· Anticiper les fins de vie et de support : plans de migration, suivi des échéances, demandes d'exception temporaire documentées.

· Industrialiser avec l'IaC, les pipelines, Ansible et Terraform, et automatiser la mise à jour des images de base.

· Coordonner la remédiation avec Claranet et les équipes Sécurité.

Supervision de la remédiation applicative (~20 %)

· Administrer et améliorer la chaîne d'analyse de code dans les pipelines : SAST, SCA/dépendances, détection de secrets, scan IaC, DAST.

· Définir et faire appliquer des quality gates et security gates, avec des politiques de blocage par sévérité et par ligne métier.

· Qualifier les alertes, éliminer les faux positifs et instruire les dérogations (durée, justification, validation).

· Piloter la correction par les équipes de dev : affectation, suivi des SLA par sévérité, relances, escalades et revues périodiques par application et par squad.

· Produire des tableaux de bord et des synthèses pour le management : backlog, âge moyen des vulnérabilités, respect des SLA, tendances mensuelles.

· Présenter les tendances en réunion avec les devs, les PO et la sécurité.

· Accompagner et former les développeurs : guides de code sécurisé, patterns récurrents, sensibilisation.

· Contribuer aux processus Change et Incident, ainsi qu'à la veille et à l'alerte CVE sur les composants critiques.

Hors périmètre : le support utilisateur niveau 1 et les tests fonctionnels applicatifs.

· Vous avez déjà travaillé sur des sujets de gestion des vulnérabilités, de patch management, d'administration middleware ou d'exploitation sécurisée d'environnements techniques.

· Vous êtes capable de coordonner plusieurs équipes sans lien hiérarchique direct, de documenter précisément les actions réalisées et de faire avancer les plans de remédiation jusqu'à leur mise en production.

· Une expérience dans un environnement soumis à de fortes contraintes de conformité, d'audit ou de sécurité - en banque ou en assurance - constitue un réel atout.

· 4 à 7 ans en ingénierie système ou DevSecOps, avec une spécialisation en sécurité applicative ou gestion des vulnérabilités.

· Certifications appréciées mais non obligatoires : CKA, CKS, AZ-500, Security+, CEH, OSCP

· Middleware : Tomcat, JBoss/WildFly, IIS, WebSphere, Node.js, Apache, Nginx, MQ, Corretto

· OS et conteneurs : Linux, Windows Server, Docker, Kubernetes/AKS, durcissement d'images

· Gestion des vulnérabilités : CVSS, EPSS, KEV, CVE/NVD, SBOM CycloneDX/SPDX, cycle de patch

· Outils sécurité : GitHub Advanced Security, Qualys, Artifactory, MDASH

· CI/CD : GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, security gates

· Automatisation : PowerShell, Terraform, Ansible

· Cloud : Azure, Defender for Cloud, Key Vault, ACR, Landing Zone Secrets, CyberArk/Conjur, comptes de service, rotation

Fruggr est une entreprise à mission qui accompagne les organisations vers un numérique plus performant, plus accessible et plus respectueux des personnes et de la planète.

  • Labellisés GreenTech Innovation (label du Ministère de la Transition Écologique) et inscrits dans l'Économie Sociale et Solidaire (ESS)
  • Sélectionnés par le Mouvement Impact France dans son classement Impact 120

Nos Activités

  • Fruggr, notre solution SaaS, une plateforme qui permet aux entreprises de piloter leur performance ESG IT, leur accessibilité numérique et leur gouvernance de l'IA.
  • Transformation sur les usages de l'IA, nous aidons les entreprises à déployer une intelligence artificielle responsable, maîtrisée et conforme aux exigences réglementaires (AI Act…).
  • Développement web, mobile et applicatif responsable, nous concevons des solutions numériques durables, accessibles et inclusives.

Description Du Poste

Le poste

Vous rejoignez l'équipe produit de Fruggr, à Nantes. Vous y développez les fonctionnalités de Fruggr, notre plateforme SaaS : gouvernance de l'IA, accessibilité numérique et Digital Workplace.

Ce qu'on attend de vous, ce n'est pas d'écrire le plus de lignes de code possible. C'est de résoudre les bons problèmes, avec les bons outils et avec l'équipe. Chez nous, travailler avec quelqu'un, c'est travailler avec deux interlocuteurs : la personne et son IA. Vous savez parler aux deux.

Concrètement, l'IA fait partie de notre méthode de travail quotidienne : vous écrivez les specs, l'agent code, vous validez, vous livrez. Et vous challengez les choix de la machine pour tirer le meilleur de ce binôme.

Vos activités au quotidien

  • Comprendre le besoin d'une PO ou d'un client et le traduire en spécifications claires, exploitables par l'équipe et par ses agents IA.
  • Concevoir, développer et faire évoluer les fonctionnalités du produit, en choisissant la technologie la plus adaptée au problème posé.
  • Travailler au quotidien avec des outils d'IA (Claude Code, Spec-Driven Development, harnais de développement), en gardant un regard critique sur ce que produit la machine.
  • Aider vos collègues à tirer le meilleur de l'IA dans leur façon de travailler : partager vos pratiques, débloquer les situations, rendre les choses simples.
  • Participer au support produit en rotation avec les autres développeureuses : investiguer, diagnostiquer et résoudre les incidents remontés par les clients.
  • Contribuer aux choix d'architecture et à la qualité de la plateforme.

L'environnement technique

Le produit tourne aujourd'hui principalement en TypeScript (Node.js, React), avec du GraphQL, sur Azure.

Vous ne maîtrisez pas ces technologies ? Ce n'est pas un prérequis. Avec l'IA, le langage devient un outil parmi d'autres : ce qui compte, c'est votre expérience du développement et votre capacité à choisir la bonne techno selon le contexte. Vous venez de .NET, de Java, de Python ou d'ailleurs et vous avez envie d'élargir votre horizon ? Votre candidature nous intéresse.

Profil recherché

  • Au moins 3 ans d'expérience en développement, avec plusieurs projets menés de bout en bout.
  • Un vrai bagage de développeureuse : vous avez pratiqué plusieurs langages ou environnements et savez justifier vos choix techniques.
  • Une pratique concrète de l'IA dans votre travail de développement. Pas besoin d'être experte, mais vous savez ce qu'est le Spec-Driven Development ou un harnais de développement, et vous connaissez les forces et les limites de ces outils.
  • Une expérience dans un contexte produit est un vrai plus : vous comprenez en quoi les enjeux diffèrent de ceux d'un projet en prestation.
  • Un grand sens de la pédagogie. Vous savez vulgariser, vous adapter à votre interlocuteur et expliquer un sujet technique à quelqu'un qui n'est pas développeur.
  • Un esprit d'équipe affirmé. Vous êtes proactifve face aux problèmes et vous préférez avancer avec les autres plutôt que seule dans votre coin.
  • L'envie de faire partie de la vie de l'équipe nantaise, avec une présence dans nos locaux 2 à 3 jours par semaine.

Vous ne cochez pas toutes les cases mais le poste vous parle ? Certaines compétences s'acquièrent en chemin : n'hésitez pas à postuler.

Démarrage

Pas d'urgence : si vous avez un préavis de 3 mois, ce n'est pas un problème.

Process de recrutement

  • Un premier échange RH pour parler de votre parcours, de vos motivations et de vos attentes.
  • Un entretien technique avec un membre de l'équipe : vos expériences, votre façon de travailler avec l'IA et votre approche des problèmes.
  • Un entretien avec une responsable de l'activité

Avantages

  • Télétravail

WHY THIS ROLE, NOW


Vocca is 2 years old. Our AI answers the phone for medical practices so they never miss a patient call again, and it already handles 70% of calls without a human. Revenue grew 3x in the last 6 months and we are opening the US. The product works. The next 12 months are about scaling it, and a call only counts as handled if the appointment lands in the clinic's software. That is this role.


THE PROBLEM YOU WILL SOLVE


Every medical practice runs on software that holds its calendar and its patients. There are dozens of different ones. Most were built twenty years ago and some have no API at all. To book an appointment during a call, our AI agent has to read and write in that software in real time, while the patient waits on the line. Nobody else has managed to build this. On several of these systems, Vocca is the only integrator in the world.

This is the work with the most direct impact on the business. A clinic whose software is connected to our agent does not switch. Retention, pricing power, our lead over competitors: it all depends on these integrations. Every software we cannot connect is a clinic we cannot sign.

The next step is writing back. Today the agent reads and books. Tomorrow it updates records in EHR, PMS and RIS systems, which raises the reliability bar a lot. In the US, we are opening the dental software ecosystem, with the compliance work that comes with it (HIPAA, SOC2).

The long term vision is simple: the agent becomes the action layer between patients and everything the front desk used to do by hand. The integrations are the road to get there. You would be building that road.


WHAT YOU WILL OWN


  • The architecture of our booking layer. Today it is code written provider by provider, under pressure. It is becoming one unified layer in TypeScript that can handle the rules of each medical centre and where adding a new software takes days, not weeks.
  • Speed and reliability at more than 1 million calls a month. A call to a clinic software can take several seconds, and the patient cannot wait. You decide how we detect a booking failure in a clinic within 24 hours and what a healthy integration looks like.
  • The hard integrations that nobody else wants to do. They are what makes Vocca hard to replace.
  • The decisions on your scope. You decide which software we connect first, with the sales, ops and support teams and the clinics themselves, and you prove it worked with a number: bookings that go through, failures caught, clinics signed.
  • The next hires. You take part in hiring the engineers who join after you, and you help them ship in their first week.


HOW WE BUILD


  • We are experimental, not R&D. You test, you prove with data, you ship. Challenging a decision means coming back with a number.
  • We ship the version that works, then fix the last 1% when it shows up. With AI, this trade off is much cheaper than before. But the judgment about what not to touch is yours.
  • We use AI seriously. Agents in every workflow, Claude Max provided. A migration estimated at 3 months was done in 2 weeks.
  • You talk every day with the ops team that deploys clinics, the support team that hears when something breaks and, when it matters, the clinics and the software vendors themselves.


STACK


TypeScript everywhere (Node, monorepo), PostgreSQL, REST and SOAP APIs from software vendors. We are migrating our last Python services to TypeScript over the coming months.


WHO DOES WELL HERE


  • You have built something that mattered: an early engineer at a startup that took off, a founding engineer, a system you launched that real users depended on. You can tell us who it was for, what problem it solved and which number moved.
  • You have integrated systems you did not control and you know the difference between a clean API and the real world.
  • 4+ years building backend systems in production, mostly in startups or fast growing companies where you had to decide with incomplete information.
  • Strong in TypeScript and Node. Or a strong backend engineer in Go, Python or Java who is clearly ready to become strong in TypeScript.
  • Solid engineering habits: system design, clean refactoring and a good nose for the risks of generated code that nobody tested.
  • You can say no, reduce the scope and explain a technical decision to a founder in two minutes.


WHAT WE EXPECT FROM YOU


First week

  • Get onboarded on the stack.
  • Ship your first fix on a live integration.

First month

  • Own one integration end to end, from the software vendor to production, and show what it changed.
  • Write down how our booking layer should evolve.

First 3 months

  • The unified booking layer in TypeScript is the standard.
  • Adding a new software takes days, not weeks.
  • We detect a booking failure in any clinic within 24 hours.

6 to 12 months

  • Our first US integrations run in production.
  • You have hired at least one engineer and they ship on their own.


PROCESS: 4 STEPS, FAST


  1. 45 min with Nans (Talent).
  2. 30 min with Hugo (CTO) or Pierrick (Head of Engineering).
  3. 1h30 in our office: live coding without AI, a real conversation about architecture and a product case with Charles, our CPO.
  4. 30 min with the one you have not met yet.


Then references and an offer. When the match is obvious, we have made an offer in 24 hours. You get feedback at every step.

Under the product, 60+ specialist agents run continuous extraction over each customer's documents and sessions into a persistent, per-company memory: every fact dated and traced to its source sentence, contradictions kept rather than overwritten — a discipline we call Total Capture. Patent-pending since July, in context engineering.

Stack: TypeScript throughout. A NestJS API plus a separate NestJS worker on Railway, Next.js 16 / React 19 on Vercel, Postgres with Prisma, Redis and BullMQ, Pinecone, S3-compatible storage. Agents are LangChain.js / LangGraph ReAct agents on Anthropic Claude across three model tiers, with OpenAI embeddings. Every prompt body and model config lives in one versioned master file synced to LangSmith, never hardcoded in TypeScript.

I am the founder, and not an engineer — thirty years a strategy consultant, first terminal at the end of 2022. A contract developer built the first ~20,000 lines between December and February. That was the environment, not me: 45 interconnected instruction files deploying sub-agents, around 300,000 words of standing rules, orchestrated by one always-on kernel that classifies each session, auto-attaches the rules matching the files being touched, and generates sub-agentic plans for the work.
